pages.text: "I AM HERE!" Gugu, the broad-chested pigeon, banged open the shop door and shouted. All the little winter birds fluttered away from the window feeder.
Gugu leaned close to Nono's ear and shouted again. "I WANT TO SEE THE WINTER BIRDS UP CLOSE!" Nono, the smallest, roundest sparrow, covered his ears. "That hurts..."
Kiki almost dropped a cup. Nono moved far away. The window feeder was empty. Gugu was alone. "Only me left?"
Grandpa quietly sat beside Gugu. "Your loud voice frightened the winter birds." "Really? I did not know..."
"Whisper in the shop. Use your loud voice in the alley." Gugu nodded. "In the shop, whisper!"
They played whispering. "Only this loud..." Gugu barely moved the lips. Kiki, the pointy-eared cat, and Nono came close again.
One winter bird landed on the feeder, then another and another. The three watched silently. A bird pecked seeds right in front of Gugu.
Grandpa opened the door. Gugu touched the green bag strap and went outside. "YAHOO!" The sound flew over the snow.
Gugu counted on fingers. "One, whisper in the shop! Two, loud in the alley! Three, quieter if someone is startled!" Nono gave a thumbs-up.

Next day, Gugu opened the door gently. "I am here," came a whisper. Not one bird flew away. A quieter voice lets friends stay close. Nono leaned on Gugu's shoulder. Gugu smiled. "In the shop, whisper!"
